symptom: First14B run takes about183 seconds per denoising step after initialization.
verified: R9700 32GB; native FP8 operations reported in ComfyUI log.
4 of20 steps completed in roughly12 minutes.
ComfyUI system_stats reported about17GB GPU usage, while Windows per-process counters reported30.34GB dedicated plus2.29GB shared.
Dynamic VRAM was enabled in the first-run log; no out-of-memory exception occurred.
hypothesis: Dynamic VRAM's residency accounting on this Windows configuration is allowing GPU memory pressure and paging that slows this larger model.
prediction: Disabling dynamic VRAM alone should make allocator accounting closer to Windows residency and reduce step time if residency pressure is the cause.
controlledChange: Restart only the task-owned ComfyUI process with --disable-dynamic-vram. Keep model files, precision, prompts,seed,frame count,resolution,CFG,sampler and steps unchanged.
certainty: Not a proven root cause. Reduced shared allocation is observed, but it does not establish that the original run was paging.
followupEvidence: ComfyUI get_free_memory includes unused torch cache in its available-memory total. Windows dedicated residency includes cached allocations. The two reported usage figures must not be treated as equivalent counters.
Classic loading reduced the sampled Windows dedicated/shared allocation to25.87GB/0.10GB, compared with30.34GB/2.29GB in the dynamic run.
Later dynamic-run steps were about183 seconds; later classic-run steps are about155-159 seconds. This is a modest observed difference, not proof that memory management explains most of the runtime.
The classic run is continuing to completion with no further configuration changes.
